heroHeadline: ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL 8 DAYS AWAY (JUNE 9, JSC) — NEW GLENN EXPLOSION THREATENS MOON BASE I FALL 2026; IFT-12 INVESTIGATION ONGOING; CREW DAY 52
heroSubtitle: June 1: The Artemis III crew announcement at Johnson Space Center is 8 days away (June 9, 11 a.m. EDT, NASA+/YouTube). The four astronaut names for the redesigned LEO rendezvous-and-docking test mission (targeting late 2027) will be revealed publicly for the first time. A critical setback emerged May 29 when Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded at Cape Canaveral LC-36 during a prelaunch static fire test — destroying the rocket and damaging the only pad Blue Origin operates. Since New Glenn is the sole launch vehicle for Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance lander ($188M NASA Moon Base contract), Moon Base I's fall 2026 delivery to Shackleton Connecting Ridge is now in jeopardy pending LC-36 damage assessment and repair. The FAA's mishap investigation into Starship IFT-12 (Booster 19 boostback burn failure, May 22) remains open: IFT-13 (Ship 40 + Booster 20, V3) cannot receive a flight license until SpaceX's corrective-action report is approved — analysts project return-to-flight no earlier than July–August 2026. This further delays the orbital propellant transfer demonstration (a mandatory Artemis III HLS qualification milestone) to Q3-Q4 2026 at the earliest. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 52 post-splashdown at JSC, continuing reconditioning. The Artemis II Orion is in de-servicing at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; the heat shield ships to Marshall Space Flight Center this summer for X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions. House Appropriations full-committee markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA flat with FY2026 — rejecting the White House's 23% cut. Artemis Accords: 67 signatories (Paraguay 67th, May 7).
